name: All five CV measurements and scoring availability demo

criteria.name: Exposure and brightness
criteria.definition: The photograph is neither badly underexposed nor blown out, and the subject is readable.
criteria.evaluation_evidence: Mean luminance, the share of near-black pixels, the share of near-white pixels, and a pass or fail against configured thresholds.

criteria.name: Contrast
criteria.definition: Tonal separation is strong enough that the subject separates from the background. Both flat and harsh images should be flagged.
criteria.evaluation_evidence: Spread of luminance values, a highlight and shadow check, and a pass or fail against configured thresholds.

criteria.name: Color palette fit
criteria.definition: The photograph's dominant colors fit the configured brand palette. More color is not inherently better.
criteria.evaluation_evidence: Top dominant colors from clustering and their distances to the configured palette.

criteria.name: Framing and subject position
criteria.definition: The main subject sits deliberately near the center or along a third, with usable space around it.
criteria.evaluation_evidence: Subject position relative to the center and rule-of-thirds intersections, using an identified subject region.

criteria.name: Sharpness and subject emphasis
criteria.definition: The subject is in focus and visually dominant. Background blur is acceptable. Intentional motion is not an automatic failure.
criteria.evaluation_evidence: A blur or edge measure on the subject region compared with the background.

notes: All thresholds and weights have explicit demonstration values. They are not calibrated or approved brand standards.
settings configure analysis; params configure scoring. CV implementation and measurement names remain native to the registry.
Relative criterion priorities are preserved from the six-criterion rubric and normalized across the selected subset.
Overall scores strictly below 60 are flagged. Unavailable criteria remain explicit; available weights are renormalized by the scorer.
Framing accepts center_distance <= 0.15 OR nearest_thirds_distance <= 0.10, plus every edge margin >= 0.02, once the scoring rule is aligned.

Sharpness requires subject_laplacian_variance >= 100 AND detail_emphasis_index >= 0.20, once the scoring rule is aligned. The absolute-detail floor prevents a high relative emphasis index alone from implying focus.
Both subject criteria require a reliable subject region. Missing subjects or undefined regional measurements remain unavailable, not automatic failures.
Current scorer still expects legacy framing/sharpness measurement and parameter names. These filled native thresholds require scoring-owner alignment before those two scores can be computed.
No VLM client or inference endpoint is needed for this subset.
